hooks.text: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons.
What happens when you crush an entire sun into a city?
Graduate student Jocelyn Bell Burnell found pulsing signals nicknamed Little Green Men.

title: A Teaspoon Weighs One Billion Tons
description: Discover how crushed stellar remnants pack the mass of a sun into a city-sized sphere.

beats.text: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a dense neutron star surface, NASA, 2018

beats.text: Neutron stars are the gravitationally collapsed cores of massive stars formed following a supernova explosion.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory image of Cassiopeia A supernova remnant, 2004

beats.text: In nineteen sixty-seven, graduate student Jocelyn Bell Burnell detected a radio pulse so rhythmic she nicknamed it Little Green Men.
beats.visual: Photograph of Jocelyn Bell Burnell with radio telescope equipment, 1967

beats.text: These stellar remnants pack the mass of a sun into a sphere only twelve miles wide.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating neutron star size compared to Manhattan, NASA, 2015

beats.text: The extreme objects rotate hundreds of times per second and generate magnetic fields trillions of times stronger than Earth's.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a rotating pulsar beaming radiation, NASA, 2016

beats.text: In twenty seventeen, scientists finally heard two of them collide through gravitational waves.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of two neutron stars merging in a kilonova, NSF, 2017

beats.text: These cosmic impacts created the heavy gold and platinum found in our jewelry today, leaving behind a single teaspoon of material that weighs one billion tons.
beats.visual: Photograph of gold bullion bars and platinum nuggets, 2020

better_than_last: Shortened the hook to 11 words to strictly meet the under-12-word rule while maintaining the powerful numerical punch.
